focus: Producers of the path-drift and template-source classes
noveltyJustification: Five of six findings are fully new (the move sequence, the refresh-only post-step, restore symmetry, the repair boundary, generator compilation dependency); one confirms the iteration-2 hypothesis and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Writing a new path-repair tool instead of invoking repair-derived.cjs

label: archive.sh moves a packet by cp -R to a temp target, atomic mv into z_archive/, then rm -rf of the source, and afterwards calls only refresh_track_root; it never calls repair-derived.cjs, so the moved packet's own recorded paths (description.json specFolder, graph-metadata.json spec_folder, document packet_pointer) keep their pre-archive values.

The same script proves the right pattern: refresh_track_root runs refresh-track-roots.mjs --apply and warns with a copy-pasteable remediation when the script is missing; the packet's own re-derive is simply absent from the same post-move sequence.
restore_spec has the same shape: mv back to the packet home then refresh_track_root only, so both directions of the move reintroduce path drift.

repair-derived.cjs already owns this class: it recomputes the recorded folder name, frontmatter packet pointer, missing level in the generated description, and stale generated-metadata fingerprints; reporting is the default, writes require --apply, exit 0 means nothing to repair, 1 repairable work found while reporting, 2 a failed repair.

The repair boundary is explicit: derived facts may be rewritten; authored facts (evidence, verification results, decisions, handover accounts) may not, and roughly 139 packets / 1,100 rule instances fail for authored reasons and should keep failing. Any heal-on-upgrade path must inherit this refusal.

create.sh derives graph-metadata paths at creation from the folder path (relative_spec strip of the specs root) and writes description.json through a compiled dist artifact (dist/spec-folder/generate-description.js); a checkout without a build gets a partially-scaffolded warning, so creation-time derivation plus later moves plus missing builds are the entry points for drift.
create.sh already names 'repair-derived.cjs --folder <packet> --apply' as its remedy when generators are missing, so the tool is acknowledged in the creation path but not in the move path.

reason: repair-derived.cjs already owns the recomputation with a dry-run default, batched --folder support and a documented refusal boundary; the gap is invocation, not capability.
